messages.subject: %variance
parts:
Hello all:

I've identified a single QTL in a mouse F2 using "scanone". To get
estimates of a and d I used "fitqtl". The fitqtl model was y~Q1+SEX+HG
+CROSS (SEX, HG and CROSS are covariates also used in "scanone").
When I compare the %variance for the QTL term from the resulting
fitqtl ANOVA table, it is roughly half of what I get using the
formula, %Var=(100(1-10^(-2LOD / n))). Why the discrepancy? I'm I
interpreting this incorrectly?

Thanks,
Charles

messages.subject: Re: %variance
parts:
Saunak Sen just explained this, but I was virtually done with my own
explanation,
and so I submit the following, even though it is redundant.

Let's ignore the missing genotype data issue, and pretend that we are
thinking
about multiple linear regression. There are three models to think
about:

full: y = intercept + Q + sex + hg + cross + error
reduced: y = intercept + sex + hg + cross + error
null: y = intercept + error

Let RSS_f, RSS_r, and RSS_0 denote the residual sum of squares under
these three
models. There are three LOD scores that are of interest:

LOD_f = (n/2) log10( RSS_0 / RSS_f )
LOD_r = (n/2) log10( RSS_0 / RSS_r )
LOD_fvr = (n/2) log10( RSS_r / RSS_f ) = LOD_f - LOD_r

In the "drop one term at a time" table in the summary of the fitqtl
output,
LOD_fvr is displayed.

The estimated percent variance explained by the QTL is (RSS_r -
RSS_f) / RSS_0
= RSS_r/RSS_0 - RSS_f/RSS_0 = 10^[-(2/n) LOD_r] - 10^[-(2/n) LOD_f].

karl
